children: revealed the roadmap for Nexus, a platform for building and deploying applications through its fault-tolerant quantum computer, Apollo, which is slated for release in 2029.
Nexus is designed to be the first developer platform that integrates automated error-correction encoding, execution on Quantinuum hardware, and hybrid workflow orchestration.

"Our aim is to build the first developer platform specifically for the fault-tolerant era so customers can start developing applications today and carry that investment forward," said Quantinuum CEO Rajeeb Hazra. "Nexus is designed to help them deploy applications and hybrid workflows and integrate the platform into their computing environments. As our systems become more capable, our aim is for the applications, workflows, and expertise customers develop in Nexus to become more valuable, giving them a compelling reason to build with Quantinuum and making Nexus an enduring part of their computing environment."
The company is already working with scores of organizations on its Nexus platform. Those wanting to participate can apply here.
Quantinuum shares had dropped 10% by noon trading on Thursday along with most other quantum stocks and the market in general. Infleqtion
Quantinuum will release its third quarter financial results post-market on Thursday.

title: Quantinuum reveals developer platform roadmap for its upcoming fault-tolerant quantum system
